thread:
jamie (eng-ml): heads up — want to triage a new community model request from a partner. repo: https://github.com/openbench/astral-12b. asking to serve in Dedicated for pilot. can we onboard? :eyes:

maria (legal): can you paste the license and confirm weights source? quick note: if license is NC or ND, hosting/quantization might be blocked.

jamie (eng-ml): here are the top lines from the repo README and license header:
```
Model: astral-12b-v2
Weights: included (checkpoint.tar.gz)
License: CC-BY-NC-ND-2.0
Note: "NoDerivatives" and "NonCommercial" — upstream prohibits commercial use and redistribution/modification.
```
Link: https://github.com/openbench/astral-12b/blob/main/LICENSE.txt

compliance-bot: automated scan results -> license: CC-BY-NC-ND-2.0; flags: ["non-commercial", "no-derivatives"]; recommended action: legal review required for hosting or quantization.

alex (infra): size looks ~98GB frozen checkpoint. If legal says OK, infra needs to know if we can store weights in our hosted buckets or only allow Private VPC. Also quantization pipeline touches weights so ND could be an issue.

liz (product): product team has a customer pilot wanting lower-latency hosted inference next quarter. If license blocks hosted, we need to surface alternatives. Prioritization: do we try to get a commercial license or pivot?

maria (legal): summary from my side: CC-BY-NC-ND explicitly forbids commercial use and creating derivatives. Quantization is a modification of the weights and likely constitutes a derivative. Hosting a hosted API that charges customers = commercial use. So current license prevents both hosted and commercial dedicated offers. Private on-prem deployment by customer is ambiguous: if customer has the weights and runs them in their environment without us redistributing, that may be allowed, but we need the exact license text and provenance.

maria (legal): questions for jamie:
- origin of weights: were they trained from public datasets or third-party licensed data? any third-party checkpoints used?
- any CLA/contact for upstream authors to request a commercial license?

jamie (eng-ml): weights came from the repo tarball. author is listed as @openbench-author (contact email in repo). no sign of third-party checkpoints. I can ping upstream for clarification and a commercial license option.

maria (legal): next steps from legal:
- get upstream contact and ask for a commercial license or explicit permission for quantization/modification + hosting.
- capture author statement about dataset provenance and export control (any restricted data or sourced from regulated corpora).
- if authors decline, we cannot serve on Redwood-hosted or charge for usage. Private deploy might still be possible if the customer holds the weights and we only deliver orchestration (need to review our terms and whether that counts as redistribution).

alex (infra): ops checklist items if legal gets greenlight:
- verify checksum and provenance of weights before ingest.
- quarantine initial checkpoint in staging S3 with restricted ACLs.
- run quantization in isolated env, keep original immutable.
- ensure model card + license is surfaced in Console and API responses (transparency).

liz (product): prioritization decision: two paths — (A) pursue upstream commercial license (timebox 2 weeks), (B) propose alternative permissively-licensed model (we'll ID 2 candidates). I'll brief sales/customer.

jamie (eng-ml): I've emailed upstream asking for a commercial license and permission to quantize; cc'ing legal. will paste reply here. assigning myself to follow up.

maria (legal): also flagging export-control review. if upstream or dataset contains EU/US sanctioned country data or restricted tech, we need compliance signoff. I'll open a soft ticket with compliance team now.

jamie (eng-ml): noted. temporary status: HOLD for hosted/dedicated until legal confirms. moving to "paperwork" stage. thanks all :thumbsup:
